A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, and principal experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables, and figures can be matched across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original restoration experiments, ablations, semantic-consistency analyses, user studies, and five-seed training-stability results.

after.justification: V3 retains original restoration experiments and user studies, and reports additional OCR, face-verification, and GyroBlur results.

M1.justification: The OSEDiff-generated variants, Gaussian-basis frequency masks, conditional weighting, training losses, and ORNet architecture remain unchanged. Sections 3–4 and the appendix describe the same training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: V3 adds GyroBlur-Synth and GyroBlur-Real evaluation, extending coverage to synthetic and real motion-blur data associated with gyroscope measurements. Its quantitative semantic evaluation also switches from object-detection consistency to OCR and face verification, introducing distinct downstream task requirements. Existing GoPro, SIDD, HIDE, and LOL coverage remains.

E2.justification: GyroDeblurNet is newly compared with its ORNet-refined output in v3 Table 9. Within the revised hallucination comparison, Table 5 replaces the super-resolved-GT comparator with original GT for OCR. The principal restoration baselines in Table 1 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 replaces the quantitative fidelity protocol: v1 uses CLIP similarity and YOLOv8 detections referenced to original-GT predictions, whereas v3 uses 83 manually labeled OCR samples with EasyOCR and 566 face-verification samples with InsightFace at a cosine threshold of 0.5. This substantially changes the evaluation design; established training, user-study, and synthetic-degradation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The hallucination diagnostic is revised to test text preservation and facial identity, replacing the aggregate CLIP/object-detection analysis while retaining Figure 7's illustrative CLIP comparison. Existing mask-design, scale-factor, basis-count, enhancement-strength, direct-ISR, and finetuning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five independent ORNet training runs with distinct seeds and identical metric standard deviations in Section 8.7. V3 adds no uncertainty estimates or significance-testing procedures for its new evaluations.

E6.justification: Table 5's aggregate CLIP/detection results are replaced by OCR precision/recall of 0.9287/0.9249 for enhanced GT versus 0.9130/0.9104 for original GT, plus 100% face verification and 0.9133 average cosine similarity. New Table 9 reports GyroBlur results, including real-set MUSIQ of 49.75 versus 69.75 with ORNet. Matched pre-existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the Gaussian-mask definitions, frequency-fusion formulation, and loss objectives are mathematically unchanged. Neither the main text nor the appendices add formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about enhanced supervision, semantic preservation through frequency mixup, and lightweight model-agnostic refinement. Removing 'consistently' from one abstract sentence does not redefine claims retained elsewhere.

C2.justification: V1 interprets CLIP/detection agreement as evidence of semantic fidelity and downstream reliability. V3 instead argues that success on structurally sensitive OCR and face-verification tasks confirms authentic texture restoration without hallucinated artifacts. The substantive limitations concerning enhancement-strength selection and inadequate fidelity metrics remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the explicit code-repository link with a project-page link; the PDFs do not establish whether code availability changed. It also documents region extraction, manual OCR labeling, evaluation tools, and the verification threshold for the new analyses. Existing architecture and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including ICM-SR, Robust Image Denoising through Adversarial Frequency Mixup, and Gyro-based Neural Single Image Deblurring. These expand relevant citations without substantially changing the paper's novelty positioning or relationship to existing restoration methods.

P1.justification: V3 corrects spelling and grammar, standardizes several headings, adds acknowledgements, and locally rewrites the hallucination-validation passage. The overall narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 is redesigned for OCR and face-verification metrics, and a new GyroBlur table is inserted. Appendix tables are renumbered, supplementary prefixes are removed, and figures and text reflow across pages. Existing figure examples and most table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The manually labeled OCR evaluation and identity checks provide more direct evidence about semantic preservation than v1's aggregate similarity proxies, while GyroBlur adds useful generalization evidence. These are limited gains: the earlier quantitative comparison is dropped, recognition success does not establish the absence of all hallucinated textures, and Section 9 still describes the superseded detection-based Table 5. Overall, v3 modestly strengthens empirical support without changing the method or established restoration results.
